lines.speaker: BELL
lines.script_text: I never left the door, sir. I swear to God. I heard him moving around in there all night. Drawers. Footsteps. (beat) Around two I knocked, just to check on him. Three times, soft. Didn't want to wake the floor. (beat) Then screaming. Then nothing.

lines.speaker: BELL
lines.script_text: Door was bolted from the inside. By the time the super opened it— (he looks up at the window)

lines.speaker: WARD
lines.script_text: Maybe he was packing. Or maybe the Judge wanted it to look that way.

lines.speaker: WARD
lines.script_text: The Judge came in through the window. Pryce ran. The ice did the rest.

lines.speaker: WARD
lines.script_text: Nobody came through that door. So he came through the window.

lines.speaker: FENN
lines.script_text: Terrible. Terrible thing. (beat) You know, a fella came by the night before last. Late. Flashed a badge. Said he was from the city, checking the boiler. I let him down in the basement.

lines.speaker: FENN
lines.script_text: Tall. Long coat. (shrugs) I looked at the badge, not the face.

lines.speaker: WARD
lines.script_text: He wasn't checking the boiler. He was looking for another way up.

lines.speaker: WARD
lines.script_text: A badge. The papers were right. The Night Judge was a cop.
